item.title: US Senate backs Trump on Iran strikes, blocks bid to limit his war powers
item.description: The US Senate votes 53 to 47 not to advance the resolution, largely along party lines, with all but one Republican voting against the procedural motion and all but one Democrat supporting it

item.title: How a single landslide shot up the price of waste in Cebu’s top cities
item.description: As officials seek accountability for the deaths in the Binaliw 'trashslide,' Cebu’s highly urbanized cities must face record-high waste management costs

item.title: House OKs ethics probe into Bong Suntay’s remarks vs Anne Curtis
item.description: 'The dignity of women should never be made the subject of humor within Congress,' says House women and gender equality chair Ann Matibag

item.title: US lawmakers raise concerns about Intel’s testing of tools from China-linked firm
item.description: 'By operating in Intel’s facilities, ACM could gain exposure to cutting-edge chipmaking processes that may materially improve the quality and competitiveness of ACM and Chinese military companies,' US lawmakers tell Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan in a letter

item.title: Top Vatican cardinal calls US-Israeli strikes ‘truly alarming’
item.description: It is unusual for Vatican diplomats to openly critique specific military campaigns. Vatican officials usually prefer to be behind the scenes, leaving open the possibility of the Church serving as mediator in conflicts.

item.title: China boosts defense spending 7% in drive to modernize by 2035
item.description: Analysts and regional military attaches are watching China's budget closely as it scrambles to modernize the military, while stepping up deployments across East Asia and purging the top brass to tackle graft

item.description: If Duterte does not submit a response, she will be considered to have made a general denial to the allegations

item.title: FACT CHECK: Trillanes not arrested over alleged ICC ‘bribe’

item.title: Higher food prices push inflation up to 2.4% in February 2026
item.description: Rice prices, in particular, are now seeing slower deflation at 3.4% in February from 8.5% in January after experiencing record deflation in 2025
